introspection

/in-tro-SPEK-shun/ — stress on SPEK · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Introspection is the act of closely examining one's own thoughts and feelings.

A week of quiet introspection helped her understand why the argument had hurt so much.

Example

After the difficult argument with her best friend, Maya spent the weekend in quiet introspection, examining her own words and feelings carefully.

Introspection emphasizes closely examining one's own thoughts and feelings, which is more precise than 'thinking about yourself' — it suggests a deep, intentional look inward at the emotional and mental layers, not just casual self-awareness.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

soul-searching: Soul-searching is a deep, often uncomfortable look at your own conscience, usually forced on you by a hard choice or a failure. Introspection is calmer and more general — a deliberate examination of your own thoughts and feelings that needs no crisis to set it off.

meditation: Meditation is a quiet, focused practice for calming and clearing the mind — often you let thoughts drift past without chasing any of them. Introspection is nearly the opposite move: you deliberately chase your own thoughts and feelings, examining where they come from and why.

analysis: Analysis means breaking something down to study its parts, and its target can be anything at all — a poem, a budget, a chess game. Introspection is analysis pointed at exactly one subject: your own thoughts and feelings, examined patiently from the inside.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

extroversion: directing your energy outward toward people and activity

thoughtlessness: acting without ever examining your own mind

Where it sits · how deeply you probe your own mind

awareness → self-awareness → introspection → obsessive self-examination

awareness vs. introspection: Awareness is much weaker than introspection: awareness just means noticing things, while introspection is a deliberate, careful examination of your own thoughts and feelings.

self-awareness vs. introspection: Self-awareness is weaker than introspection — self-awareness is knowing what you feel, while introspection is actively digging into why you feel it.

obsessive self-examination vs. introspection: Obsessive self-examination goes beyond introspection: introspection is healthy, purposeful reflection, while obsessive self-examination means picking at every thought until it becomes unhealthy.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — intro-: inward (Latin)

Root — spect: to look (Latin)

Suffix — -ion: act or process of (Latin)

Put it together: Intro- ('inward') + spect ('to look') + -ion ('act of') literally builds 'the act of looking inward' — exactly what introspection means: examining your own thoughts and feelings.

Use the root in a new word: inspect: Before buying the used bike, Theo had a mechanic inspect every bolt and brake cable first.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / academic

Introspection suggests intentional, deep self-examination — use it when someone is deliberately thinking through their own thoughts and feelings. For simple self-awareness, 'self-awareness' or 'self-reflection' is simpler.
